subject: Post-call: Aurora perf requirements — context sizes, concurrency, streaming next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Aurora perf requirements — context sizes, concurrency, streaming next steps

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can size a short POC: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary use: clinician-facing summarization + decision support in the EHR; prompts include patient history (~800–1,500 tokens) + additional structured context (med lists, vitals).
- Typical output: 150–600 tokens; some cases up to ~1,200 tokens for complex consults.
- Desired UX: streaming partial results for the summarize/diagnostic flow so clinicians see the first sentences quickly.
- Concurrency: 50 steady concurrent users during clinic hours; burst up to ~120 concurrent during handoff periods.
- Throughput target: ~3,000 inference requests per hour (avg), with peaks to ~6,000/hour.
- Security: SOC 2 + isolated VPC option under consideration (procurement).

Performance targets you mentioned:
- Target p95 infer latency (user-facing, streaming start-to-first-token) <= 500 ms for 150–600 token outputs; p95 end-to-end completion goal <= 2s for outputs <= 600 tokens.

Concrete asks / next steps from Redwood: 
1) Can you confirm average and 95th percentile input token sizes (we heard 800–1,500 tokens but need sample payloads or a small set of representative prompts)?
2) Do you require strict end-to-end completion p95 SLA for the full output, or is start-of-stream latency the more critical metric?
3) Can procurement share their questionnaire and preferred contract cadence so we can align on Dedicated vs Private options?

I've attached a lightweight sizing template (redwood_sizing_template.xlsx) — please drop a couple of representative prompts/records into tab "samples" and we will run a tokenization/profile pass and come back with two pragmatic options (Hosted with autoscale + Dedicated reserved pool estimate).

Next sync: can we pencil in a 30-minute architecture follow-up next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks —
Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: 2026-11-18T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Aurora perf requirements — context sizes, concurrency, streaming next steps

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Tokens: our telemetry shows median input ~1,200 tokens, 95th ~2,100 tokens (long consults). Outputs are typically 200–800 tokens; peak cases can be ~1,200 tokens.
2) Streaming: start-of-stream is critical for clinician workflow. If we can get first partial tokens within ~400–500ms at p95 that would be ideal; full completion SLA can be softer (we can tolerate p95 <= 4s for very long outputs).
3) Concurrency: 50 steady + 120 burst aligns with our expectations. We will also batch a small set of scheduled analysis jobs overnight (lower latency requirement but high throughput).
4) Security/procurement: procurement (cc'd) will send the standard security questionnaire and GxP appendix. We will need either Dedicated capacity or a Private deployment for PHI — please flag what evidence you can provide for the SOC 2 and network isolation.

I uploaded two sanitized prompt examples to the Drive folder you linked and added a short distribution profile (typical hour-by-hour requests). Let us know if those are sufficient.

We can do the architecture follow-up on Tuesday 11/24 at 10am PT.

Best,
Maria
Product Lead, Clinical AI
Aurora Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Aurora perf requirements — context sizes, concurrency, streaming next steps

All — quick engineering read on the ask and suggested low-friction paths.

Observations:
- Input sizes up to ~2.1k tokens and outputs up to ~1.2k (with streaming) change our tradeoffs: batching aggressively (to cut per-token cost) will increase first-token latency and hurt the streaming UX. Conversely, single-request execution favors lower start-of-stream latency but higher cost.
- We can leverage KV/prefix caching for recurring sections (e.g., patient history templates) to reduce tokenization cost on repeated requests, which helps the steady 50 concurrent case.

Two pragmatic options to propose to the customer:
1) Hosted API + streaming-first config (recommended for fast time-to-value):
   - Configure streaming with small early-send thresholds (emit first 32–64 tokens as soon as available).
   - Autoscale worker pool to handle bursts; set soft concurrency limit per-worker to preserve start latency.
   - p95 start-of-stream target: 350–500ms (depends on model pick). Estimate cost: higher per-token but minimal ops overhead.

2) Dedicated reserved pool (for PHI/isolation + predictable latency):
   - Reserve a cluster sized for baseline 50 concurrency with headroom for 120 bursts (suggest baseline = 6 model-serving GPUs with fast NVMe for KV cache).
   - Use quantized model variant for throughput jobs and a full-precision variant for the clinician interactive flow if content quality requires it.
   - p95 start-of-stream target: 200–350ms with dedicated nodes and tuned kernels. Lower cost at scale but requires commit.

POC plan (recommended):
- Customer drops 10–20 representative requests in the sizing sheet (they already uploaded two; ask for 8–10 more covering long-tail).
- We run a small synthetic load (burst + steady) against a matching model profile and return a performance matrix: start-of-stream p50/p95, completion p50/p95 for 200/600/1200 token outputs, and cost per 1k requests.
- Timebox: 5 business days to run and deliver results once samples received.

Technical ask for the call on 11/24: please have someone from Aurora engineering join for a short sketch of the EHR integration and expected network topology (VPC peering / egress constraints). Also ask procurement to surface the SOC2 evidence they need — we can pre-populate common artifacts.

I'll draft a short SLO options doc and drop it into the shared Drive before the Tuesday call.

-Jordan
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — great, thanks for the samples and the profile. We're aligned on the streaming-first constraint. Next steps and deliverables from Redwood: 

1) Sizing & Options (attached): we ran an initial tokenization pass on the samples you uploaded and sketched two options: Hosted streaming-first baseline and Dedicated reserved pool. See attached SLA-proposal-Aurora-v1.pdf for latency/availability tradeoffs and an estimate range.
2) POC offer: 5-business-day performance sweep (no charge) once you confirm 8 more representative prompts in the sizing sheet. We will measure: first-token p50/p95, completion p50/p95 for 200/600/1200 tokens, concurrency behavior at 50 and 120, and streaming fidelity under 10% packet loss simulation.
3) Security: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report, network topology templates for a VPC deployment, and a sample Data Processing Addendum. Procurement: Monica can connect you to our Security team if you confirm the required artifacts.

Please confirm:
- Can Aurora add 8 more representative prompts to the redwood_sizing_template.xlsx (tab: samples) by EOD Friday 11/21?
- Is Tuesday 11/24 10am PT still good for the architecture sync (we'll include one of our security engineers for 10–15 min)?

If yes on both, we'll kick off the internal POC planning and share a brief test plan by EOD Monday.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Monica

Monica.Patel@redwood.ai
